title: Velocity harness for multi-protocol streaming chat (SSE + WS) with p95 regression detection
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description: Build a high-fidelity, scalable load harness that emulates heterogeneous real-world streaming chat clients over SSE and WebSocket protocols. The harness must measure token throughput (tokens/sec), end-to-end p95 latency, server-side p95, and detect regressions automatically versus a sliding baseline. The design should exercise prefix/KV cache effects, session-affinity behaviors, connection churn, and multi-tenant isolation. Outputs include time-series metrics, per-run regression reports, and a synthetic replay package for root-cause reproduction.
scenarios: Burst-y chat: 10k concurrent SSE clients with short-lived sessions, high token bursts (avg 120 tokens/session)
Steady long chat: 2k WS clients with long-lived sessions, repeated prefixes to exercise KV cache hits
Mixed tenant: 5 tenants with skewed traffic (one hot tenant at 50% of tokens), validate isolation and token quotas
Churn storm: periodic 40% connection churn every 10s to validate reconnection/backoff and KV cache re-warm
Backpressure: clients that slow-read responses to force server buffering / test memory limits
Cold-start: scale-up from 0 to target RPS in 5 minutes to capture cold-queue behaviors
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run SSE and WS scenarios from a single config file and produce consistent time-series outputs
Automated regression detection compares new run to N-day baseline and raises a PR/alert when p95 increases > 15% or tokens/sec drops > 10%
Results produce a deterministic replay artifact (seeded prompts + timing) to reproduce a failing run locally
KV cache-aware probes show cache hit ratios and ability to tag requests that require cold vs warm KV paths
Integration with Grafana + Alertmanager for thresholded alerts and with CI for gating merges to runtime-1.22
Runbook documented and run executed successfully at 10k simulated clients in staging with expected resource usage
implementation_notes: Client generator will be implemented in Go with gRPC control plane; workers create lightweight goroutines per session to mimic realistic socket behavior
Use a hybrid driver: real WebSocket connections for fidelity, SSE for scale (SSE clients multiplexed where feasible)
Token pacing should be configurable: deterministic token emission schedule + probabilistic jitter to mimic human typing
Embed a small set of canonical prompt families to exercise system prompts, tool-calls, and long-form completions; seeds stored in bucket for replay
Telemetry tagged with scenario, tenant_id, seed_id, session_id; export to Prometheus histograms and OTLP traces for p95 reconstruction
Regression detection uses a rolling 7-day baseline with Holt-Winters smoothing to suppress noise; thresholds parameterized per-metric
Support both synthetic clients (fast, scaled) and real-browser emulation for a sample subset to validate front-end integration
Resource throttles for generators to avoid saturating driver hosts; autoscaler for harness workers based on desired client concurrency
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): single-node run with 200 clients to validate semantics and telemetry tagging
Phase 2 (staging): 2k clients, run 3 scenario types, verify dashboards and regression alarms
Phase 3 (pre-prod): 10k clients mixed-protocol run, capture full baseline, iterate thresholds
Phase 4 (CI gating): wire regression detector to PR pipeline for runtime-1.22; block merges that introduce >15% p95 regressions
Phase 5 (ops): scheduled weekly runs; integrate synthetic runs into on-call rotation; add automatic Slack alert + high-priority ticket generation

2026-03-04 Marco Ruiz (review): Suggest adding tenant skew scenarios and explicit quota breach tests. Also recommend storing deterministic seed bundles to S3 for run parity.
2026-03-07 Design review: UX wants a comparison table output (baseline vs run) and a linkable replay artifact for incident tickets. Agreed to include an auto-generated HTML summary per run.
